Enforced by backend/tests/test_claims_are_anchored.py (contract C10). contract:<clause> resolves in docs/design/CONTRACTS.md; evidence:<text> appears in docs/EVIDENCE.md; boundary:<why> requires the sentence to carry its own limit; descriptive:<why> means it makes no claim about this gateway; debt:<clause> means it is true as qualified and the clause is what would make it unconditional.

claims.claim: The ledger's transitions carry **Z3-checked invariants showing that the modelled reserve → settle transitions cannot double-count funds** — a proof over the money model, not over the deployment.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1
claims.note: the P subset; the sentence says the proof is over the model

claims.claim: Stratoclave is a self-hosted **inference gateway** that sits in the data path in front of Amazon Bedrock and adds the three things raw Bedrock does not give you on its own: **who called which model, under whose budget, and through which identity** — enforced *before* the model is invoked, on every single request.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1
claims.note: 'enforced before the model is invoked, on every request'

claims.claim: ### The narrow thing this project is for: a proven invariant on pre-flight budget enforcement
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1
claims.note: the heading names the proved invariant

claims.claim: That makes per-tenant cost control not a nice-to-have but the P&L core, and it is a distributed-systems problem: *record the billable event across a trust boundary, exactly once, against the right tenant, non-repudiably*.
claims.anchor: descriptive:states the distributed-systems problem in the abstract

claims.claim: Stratoclave's differentiator is narrow, and it is a **guarantee level, not a feature nobody else has**: it reserves a tenant dollar pool **+** per-user token quota **+** per-model dollar quota in a **single DynamoDB `TransactWriteItems` before the model is invoked**.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.2
claims.note: every configured limit in one TransactWriteItems

claims.claim: There is no client bypass and no check-then-act (TOCTOU) overspend race — an overshoot loses the conditional write and gets a `402`.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1

claims.claim: A credential broker cannot do this at all — nothing is in the data path, so there is no request-time point to enforce at.
claims.anchor: descriptive:about the credential-broker architecture

claims.claim: LiteLLM's admission counter is a `DualCache` (in-process + Redis) with the database as an authority that catches up; whether the ceiling holds through cache loss is not something we have verified, and we do not assert that it fails.
claims.anchor: boundary:'we do not assert that it fails' — the property is stated unverified

claims.claim: Stratoclave puts the admission and the money move in the *same* authoritative store — a conditional DynamoDB transition — and carries Z3-checked invariants over that transition model showing it cannot double-count funds.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1
claims.note: scoped to the transition model in the sentence

claims.claim: Having a reservation and having a *machine-checked invariant* on the model of that reservation are different guarantee levels; this project provides the second one.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1

claims.claim: Neither the implementation nor DynamoDB's own behaviour is inside the proof — see [EVIDENCE.md](docs/EVIDENCE.md) for where each claim actually stands.
claims.anchor: boundary:names exactly what is outside the proof

claims.claim: **Shipped** — dedicated append-only ledger table; each money move (RESERVE/SETTLE/RELEASE/RECLAIM/LATE_SETTLE) is one event, duplicate-proof by a conditional write on its own key. RESERVE and the terminals are written in the same `TransactWriteItems` as the counter they move; the release path is two writes with the reaper as backstop, so a crash between them leaves the hold to be reclaimed rather than losing the event
claims.anchor: boundary:'the release path is two writes with the reaper as backstop' states the limit

claims.claim: It is their configuration, not a guarantee either project makes to the other; Stratoclave's own failure behaviour is specified in [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](./docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
claims.anchor: boundary:'not a guarantee either project makes' and it points at where the behaviour IS specified

claims.claim: Its money transitions carry a machine-checked invariant that double-counting cannot occur.
claims.anchor: contract:C3.4

claims.anchor: evidence:The limit no timing calculation removes

claims.claim: ## Why a gateway? (what a credential broker cannot do)
claims.anchor: descriptive:a section heading

claims.claim: That single architectural choice is what unlocks the following, none of which a broker can offer because it has no request-time choke point:
claims.anchor: descriptive:about brokers

claims.claim: - **Budget enforced *per request*, before the call — not after.** Every call reserves `max_tokens + input_estimate` with a conditional DynamoDB write *before* Bedrock is invoked, and refunds the unused remainder afterwards.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1

claims.claim: - **App-layer model / capability policy.** The model allowlist, and (on the roadmap) per-tenant reasoning-effort and tool caps, are enforced in the request handler.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.6
claims.note: roadmap items are marked as such in the sentence

claims.claim: IAM can allow or deny a *model ARN*, but it cannot express "this tenant may not use `reasoning.effort = xhigh`".
claims.anchor: descriptive:about what IAM can express

claims.claim: - **Two-level credit governance, enforced pre-flight.** Every tenant has a default credit, every user can carry a per-user override, and every inference call — to `/v1/messages` (Anthropic), `/v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI Chat), or `/openai/v1/responses` (OpenAI Responses) — reserves tokens atomically with a conditional DynamoDB write *before* Bedrock is invoked (`backend/dynamo/user_tenants.py:reserve`).
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1

claims.claim: Because the reservation is a conditional `UpdateItem`, concurrent requests that would push a balance past its limit lose the condition and are rejected — quotas cannot be raced past.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1

claims.claim: What cannot be raced past is the amount the request was ADMITTED at.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.5
claims.note: this sentence is the boundary itself

claims.claim: The bound gates admission only where the operator has turned it on (`STRATOCLAVE_HARD_CEILING_GATE`), because it also refuses requests it cannot size and an operator should measure that refusal rate on real traffic first — see [docs/design/hard-ceiling.md](docs/design/hard-ceiling.md).
claims.anchor: boundary:'only where the operator has turned it on'

claims.claim: Cost is derived from an admin-editable per-model price table (`PricingConfig`), so Opus and Haiku spend are counted differently — all in integer micro-USD, never floating point.
claims.anchor: contract:C2.5

claims.claim: A **first-event commit** rule guarantees that once the first stream byte is sent, the target is locked — a mid-stream failure never silently re-runs the model or double-bills.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.7

claims.claim: `eu-west-1`) never silently fails over into another jurisdiction.
claims.anchor: contract:C11.2

claims.claim: For single-region **data residency**, set it to a same-jurisdiction list or to **`none`** (or an empty string) **to disable failover entirely** — then a streaming request never sends prompt bytes outside the primary region.
claims.anchor: contract:C11.1

claims.claim: - **Per-model quotas + cascading model fallback.** "Use Opus until its per-model budget is gone, then Sonnet, then Haiku." Each model has an optional per-tenant (and per-user) quota, charged in the *same* atomic `TransactWriteItems` as the budget reserve — so a request can never race past a per-model limit.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.2

claims.claim: A quota is keyed on the **model**, not on the name a client used for it: every alias and Bedrock id of one registry entry counts against one counter, so a cap cannot be dodged by respelling its subject.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.4

claims.claim: And because the routing config only ever *restricts* a request, a config the gateway cannot read is not treated as a tenant without restrictions — a task serves the last config it read, or fails closed with `503 routing_config_unavailable`.
claims.anchor: contract:C7.2

claims.claim: The pin is validated against the tenant allowlist (`403` if not allowed) and the route's wire protocol (`400` if unservable) — it is never silently substituted.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.8

claims.claim: Stratoclave's SSO flow does not parse AWS credentials and never holds an IdP refresh token.
claims.anchor: contract:C6.5

claims.claim: EC2 instance profiles are rejected by default because they cannot be attributed to a single human.
claims.anchor: boundary:'rejected by default' states the policy and its default

claims.claim: Because Stratoclave never stores an IdP refresh token, a full backend compromise cannot pivot into the customer's IAM Identity Center or SAML IdP.
claims.anchor: contract:C6.5

claims.claim: Concurrent requests that would overshoot a quota cannot race.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1

claims.claim: `UsageLogs` always records the actual spend, not the reservation.
claims.anchor: contract:C4.5

claims.claim: ### Dollar pool budgets and crash-safe accounting
claims.anchor: descriptive:a section heading

claims.claim: When a tenant has a **dollar pool** for the current period, the same reservation additionally reserves the request's cost — priced from the per-model `PricingConfig` table — as integer **micro-USD** (1 USD = 1 000 000 micro-USD; never a float, and cost is rounded *up* so a request is never under-charged).
claims.anchor: contract:C2.5
claims.note: integer micro-USD, rounded up

claims.claim: A killed request leaves its hold behind; later pooled requests run a small, bounded **sweep** that reclaims expired holds — decrement and delete in one conditional transaction, so a hold is reclaimed at most once and concurrent sweepers cannot double-credit the pool: the loser's transaction cancels.
claims.anchor: boundary:names the one way the counter can still go negative

claims.claim: So on the transactional reserve path the ledger's "exactly one terminal per hold" mutual exclusion and the frozen-rating guarantees carry over unchanged, and the only genuinely new money code is one idempotency record and the rehydrate.
claims.anchor: boundary:scopes the carry-over and names the PENDING gap

claims.claim: Idempotent authorize is enforced by an idempotency record written in the same transaction as the reserve, with a request fingerprint so reusing a key for a *different* body is a `422`, never a silent wrong replay.
claims.anchor: contract:C5.3

claims.claim: - **The key identifies the operation, byte for byte.** The idempotency record is addressed by a digest of the raw `Idempotency-Key`, so two different keys are two different operations: an earlier version sanitised the key into a sort key, which merged `invoice/a` and `invoice?a` onto one record — the second authorize then either replayed the first, reporting success for an amount that was never held, or was refused as a reused key.
claims.anchor: contract:C5.2

claims.claim: OpenAI `Chat Completions` payload on the **same** Bedrock converse backend. Streaming + tool calls. Unsupported params (`n>1`, `logprobs`, `response_format`, `image_url`) rejected with `400`, never silently dropped. Requires the `messages:send` scope.
claims.anchor: contract:C13.1

claims.claim: > For **how far each differentiating claim below is actually verified today**
claims.anchor: descriptive:a pointer to EVIDENCE.md

claims.claim: > (formal proof / gateway-live / direct baseline / moto·in-process / unverified),
claims.anchor: descriptive:lists the evidence tiers used in EVIDENCE.md

claims.claim: **No client bypass** *and* **no overspend race** — pool + per-user tokens + per-model quota reserved pre-flight in one `TransactWriteItems` (optimistic snapshot lock; overshoot loses the write → `402`). **Hard at admission**, and that is the claim: no request is admitted past the limit — the limit on the amount the request is admitted AT. Whether the settled charge stays under that amount depends on how it was priced: a byte-count bound dominates any usage the provider can report, the older token estimate does not, and the bound gates admission only where `STRATOCLAVE_HARD_CEILING_GATE` is on. It is also not a hard bound on the *bill*, because an outcome the gateway cannot observe — a read timeout, a killed process — is one the gateway cannot price. Those are now classified rather than assumed unbilled (`mvp/provider_outcome.py`), but retaining their reservations is opt-in and off by default, so today such an outcome still returns its budget. See the crash-safe row below.
claims.anchor: boundary:states that the ceiling is over the admitted amount

claims.claim: **No client bypass**, and **pre-call reservation is shipped** — `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/budget_reservation.py` (first committed 2026-04-30) reserves before the call, fails closed when the reservation cannot be written, clamps adversarial `max_tokens`, and covers seven scopes. The admission counter is a `DualCache` (in-process + Redis) with the DB as an authority that catches up; the code documents recovery paths for Redis restart / cross-pod reset. **We have not tested whether the ceiling holds through cache loss, and we do not claim it fails.** The honest difference is the guarantee level, not the presence of a reservation. Verify against the version you deploy
claims.anchor: boundary:'We have not tested whether the ceiling holds through cache loss'

claims.claim: **Deploy region is operator-chosen** (`STRATOCLAVE_REGION`; only the CLOUDFRONT-scope WAF is pinned to us-east-1). **Bedrock model region is independent** (`BEDROCK_PRIMARY_REGION`). Streaming failover is configurable (`STRATOCLAVE_FAILOVER_REGIONS`), and the default set is jurisdiction-filtered so a non-US primary never back-doors to the US. `STRATOCLAVE_RESIDENCY=strict` fails the synth if any Bedrock call region (model + failover + codex) leaves the deploy region, or if the model is a geo inference profile. **aws partition only** (GovCloud/China rejected)
claims.anchor: contract:C11.4

claims.claim: **Reproducible Savings Report** (`mvp.learning.savings`; renamed from "Savings Certificate" in [docs/SCOPE.md](docs/SCOPE.md) — "certificate" overstates what the retention and export story currently support): a per-`(tenant, day)` **counterfactual** "if you'd followed the routing advice" figure over each request's REAL billed tokens (joined to the ledger by `span_id`), escalation loss **subtracted not hidden** (`net` can be negative), coverage spend-weighted. Reproducible means replayable, not merely recomputable: the report embeds the four rate legs it priced each key at and the model resolutions it used, so `savings_cli --replay` reproduces the same figure at any later date and a rate change since issue cannot move it. A replay whose embedded basis is missing a key refuses rather than quietly pricing that row at today's rate. Detail rows beyond the stored cap are not retained, so a replay reproduces the figure and the classes, not every per-request line. Quality parity is a separate tenant eval; no saving is claimed until measured. Shadow mode emits it with zero behaviour change. Reproducible one-command demo: [`docs/demo/savings-vs-litellm.md`](docs/demo/savings-vs-litellm.md)
claims.anchor: boundary:'Reproducibility has a stated boundary'

claims.claim: The single thing neither competitor can easily replicate is the **atomic pre-flight reserve/settle with crash-safe HOLD rows and a quota-driven model cascade wired into it**.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.2

claims.claim: A broker cannot do it *by construction* — it is not in the data path, so there is no request-time point to enforce at.
claims.anchor: descriptive:about brokers

claims.claim: Comparing only *shipped* capability (not "could be built" — by that logic every product's features are possible in every other, which decides nothing), the broker's cap is a soft IAM/telemetry one because it has no request-time choke point at all, while LiteLLM and Stratoclave both reserve before the call.
claims.anchor: boundary:'only shipped capability' scopes what is being compared

claims.claim: Between those two the difference is *where the enforcing state lives* — a cache with a catching-up database, versus a single authoritative store whose transition carries a machine-checked proof that double-counting cannot occur.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1

claims.claim: **Pick Stratoclave** for an AWS-committed, Bedrock-first (self-hosted GPU / any OpenAI-compatible backend bindable to the same machine-checked transition model), single-region (operator-chosen) shop that needs hard per-tenant dollar caps enforced pre-flight so a request cannot be ADMITTED past them, and — unlike a post-hoc counter — cannot even transiently overshoot under concurrency (an application-level invariant: an atomic snapshot-locked reservation, not a database `ConditionExpression`) — e.g.
claims.anchor: contract:C1.1
claims.note: 'cannot be ADMITTED past them' is the admission clause

claims.claim: **Pick a credential broker** when you must distribute to a large fleet via MDM, need GovCloud / EU or multi-region data residency, or cannot accept any new component on the inference availability path — and post-hoc audit (Bedrock invocation logging + CloudTrail) is sufficient.
claims.anchor: descriptive:when to pick a broker instead

claims.claim: The gating insight held: **semantic routing only *proves* a cost saving once the ledger and rating layers exist** — an un-provable saving cannot be billed — so the ledger/rating work was P0 and shipped first; the router is P1.
claims.anchor: descriptive:why the ledger work preceded the router

claims.claim: ## 6. What strict mode refuses, and what it guarantees
claims.anchor: descriptive:a section heading

claims.claim: Refused at admission, before any upstream call, **in `enforced` only**:
claims.anchor: descriptive:an instruction to implementers of this design

claims.claim: - an image whose dimensions cannot be read, or an S3-referenced image

claims.anchor: descriptive:an item in the refusal list

claims.claim: That is not in tension with the rule that a high refusal *rate* is answered by a tighter bound and never by a larger limit: one is a single request that cannot fit, the other is a bound that is too loose.

claims.claim: A request whose bound cannot be computed in `measured` is recorded with the bound absent and a reason, and proceeds.

claims.anchor: boundary:'is a rule of enforced' scopes it to the mode

claims.claim: The guarantee, stated with its boundary rather than as a slogan: **for admitted requests, the pool cannot be overspent, except for two cases, both alarmed and both recorded with their own cause code — a charge whose hold was reaped before it settled, and a charge where the provider exceeded the output ceiling it was given.** Those are the visible failure modes; there are two, not one.
claims.anchor: boundary:the design document states the condition in the sentence

claims.claim: Do not write "overspend is impossible" without naming both.
claims.anchor: descriptive:an instruction to implementers of this design

claims.claim: And one limit that no rule in this document removes: **a charge landing at Bedrock and the ledger write recording it are not atomic.** If Bedrock bills a request and this process then dies, the hold is never settled, the reaper releases it, and the real spend vanishes from the ledger — after which later admissions can carry the pool past its limit with every invariant here still intact, because the ledger no longer holds the charge.
claims.anchor: boundary:the design document states the condition in the sentence

claims.claim: Say so wherever the guarantee is stated; it is the ceiling on the ceiling.
claims.anchor: descriptive:an instruction to implementers of this design

claims.claim: The principle, from which every rule below follows: **the only reason to serialise requests on a shared item is to prove that a limit was not exceeded.** Measurement needs no such proof, so measurement needs no serialisation.
claims.anchor: boundary:the design document states the condition in the sentence

claims.claim: - no conditional write, even one whose condition cannot fail — an always-true condition still costs a round trip and still contends on the item

claims.claim: The rule: **a switch applies to admissions from that moment, and the guarantee is claimed only once every pre-switch hold has settled or been reaped.** Record the switch in the ledger with its timestamp so the boundary is reconstructible, and do not halt admissions, drain, or top up — those all cost availability to buy a property that waiting gives for free.
